name: Vittal Mukunda
body:
**Problem.** Erdős #902 (Schütte): f(n) = least order of a tournament in which every n vertices are beaten by a common vertex. Classical bounds: (n+2)2^{n-1} - 1 ≤ f(n) ≤ (ln 2 + o(1)) n^2 2^n (Szekeres–Szekeres 1965; Erdős 1963); f(1), f(2), f(3) = 3, 7, 19; f(4) ≤ 67 (QR_67), f(5) ≤ 331 (QR_331).

**Results (full proofs in the PDF).**
1. $f(4) \ge 52$, proved by hand. Stronger: every tournament on at most 51 vertices has a triple with at most 4 common dominators. At 51 vertices such a tournament would have to be doubly regular (a congruence mod 4 plus a spectral argument), and a third-moment identity excludes doubly regular tournaments on 51 vertices.
2. $f(n) \ge (n + 5/2)\,2^{n-1} - 1$ for all $n \ge 4$ (by hand).
3. $f(n) \ge (c^* - o(1))\, n 2^n$ with $c^* = 0.76950\ldots$, up from the constant 1/2 (by hand; uses a cross-level double-counting lemma).
4. $f(5)\ge121$, $f(6)\ge281$, $f(7)\ge665$, $f(8)\ge1485$, $f(9)\ge3388$, $f(10)\ge7398$, $f(11)\ge16569$, $f(12)\ge35655$ (exact integer recursion; the lemma behind it is proved in the paper).
5. Bipartite version: $f_{bip}(n) \ge (n+1)2^n$ (sharp for n = 1, 2) and $f_{bip}(n) \ge 2(c^*-o(1))n2^n$, via a game-value form of the Szekeres doubling. So the asymptotic bound needs no arc inside a dominator set.
6. Computer-assisted: an $S_4$ tournament on 52 vertices with no "tight" pair (a pair with exactly 11 dominators) has a vertex of in-degree ≥ 30. This uses level-7 finite-N flag-algebra certificates checked in exact rational arithmetic.

**Not claimed.** The order of magnitude of f(n) stays open (the bounds are still a factor n apart). f(4) ≥ 53 is open.

**How to check.** Sections 2–8 are complete hand proofs. Numerical steps: `python proof/verify_proof.py` (0 failures). Certificates: `python proof/search/r11/audit_b320_independent.py <cert.pkl>`, an exact verifier written independently of the solver code. The README lists every command.

**What is mine and what isn't.** The Szekeres lemma (an (n−1)-set's dominator set is undominated) and the classical bounds are due to Szekeres–Szekeres and Erdős. Bipartite variants of Schütte's problem appear in Borowiecki–Grytczuk–Hałuszczak–Tuza (2003). Results 1–6 are new as far as I know.

Each proof was audited by a separate Claude instance that did not share the derivation, and each certificate by an exact verifier written independently of the solver code.
